summary: MFA push approval attack followed by ephemeral CI token creation detected
description:
Issue summary:
A member of the engineering org reported unexpected MFA push approvals on their corporate SSO during a short window (03/13 09:12–09:20 UTC). Shortly after, we observed a CI pipeline create an ephemeral token via the internal Developer Console service (dev-console) that was used to access repositories and trigger a build.

Impact:
- Potential unauthorized access to non-prod repos and CI artifacts for a limited window.
- Several builds triggered by an ephemeral token; no obvious data exfil attempts found so far.
- A subset of services experienced increased CI runs and elevated API call volume.

Environment:
- prod us-east tenants for identity and dev-console.
- Affected accounts belong to the engineering org (org-id: redwood-eng; internal only).

Steps to reproduce / timeline of observable events:
1) 2026-03-13T09:11:58Z: External push notification deliveries spike to multiple employees (observed in auth push logs).
2) 2026-03-13T09:12:20Z: User A (reporter) receives push prompt and taps 'Approve' (claims accidental).
3) 2026-03-13T09:13:05Z: SSO shows new privileged session for User A from 185.239.1.22 (ASN linked to foreign VPN provider).
4) 2026-03-13T09:14:10Z: dev-console API creates an ephemeral CI token (token id eph-9b3f) using User A's session.
5) 2026-03-13T09:14–09:18Z: Token used to trigger 3 pipeline runs across two repos (repo-alpha, repo-infra).
6) 2026-03-13T09:20:00Z: Anomaly detection flagged unusual CI token creation pattern and rate-limited dev-console API.

Logs / evidence links:
- Auth push deliveries: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/alerts/auth-push-spike (internal link)
- SSO session events (filtered): https://logs.redwood.company/sso?q=UserA+185.239.1.22
- Dev-console audit: https://audit.redwood.company/entries?token=eph-9b3f
- CI build traces: https://ci.redwood.company/builds?token=eph-9b3f

Initial hypothesis:
- This appears to be a push-approval social engineering attack (push fatigue or deliberate prompt) where an attacker originated push notifications from an external service and induced approvals. Once an MFA approval occurred, the attacker used the session to call dev-console APIs to create ephemeral CI tokens and run builds. The goal may be to plant a CI job that later exfiltrates secrets or extends access.

Immediate business questions:
- Were any secrets or artifacts uploaded to external endpoints during the build runs?
- Can we confirm whether the ephemeral token was scoped beyond build triggering (push rights or repo write)?
- Do additional users show similar push approval activity from the same IP range?
comments: 2026-03-13 09:30 - Rahul Mehta (SRE oncall): Triage started. Rate-limited dev-console and rotated active ephemeral tokens. Notifying Security Ops. Action: block IP range 185.239.0.0/16 at edge until further review.

2026-03-13 09:45 - Maya Liu (Security): Confirmed three builds triggered by eph-9b3f. No outbound HTTP to unfamiliar domains observed in network egress logs for those builds. Pulling full build logs for artifact checks.

2026-03-13 10:05 - Sofia Hernandez (Reporter): User A reports they clicked an unexpected notification after receiving a 'verification' SMS. Provided device timestamp and list of recent notifications. We requested device screenshot and blocked session.

2026-03-13 11:00 - Dev Console Team (engineer): Temporarily disabled token-creation API for non-admin sessions and pushed a config change to require reauth for API keys created via console. Will open PR with feature flag rollback if needed. Link: https://github.com/redwood/dev-console/pull/4876

2026-03-13 12:20 - Rahul Mehta (SRE): Detected two additional users with push prompts from the same foreign ASN. Requiring org-wide forced reauth for SSO sessions created between 09:00–10:00 UTC today.
investigation_notes: Auth logs show push notifications originated from the org's push provider but were initiated via the provider API using a low-reputation API key (provider-key-zzx).
Provider API key activity traced to a rotation event last week; the key appears to have been used by a third-party integration. Working with vendor to identify requester IPs.
Ephemeral token eph-9b3f had limited scope: build.trigger, repo.read. It did not request write or secret:read scopes (based on token introspection).
No elevated GitHub PATs or service account keys were created in the window. However, one pipeline executed a script that attempted to curl to http://34.85.11.12/api/collect (blocked by egress rules).
We found a CI job step that downloads a community action from marketplace with version pin 'v1.2.3' — investigating supply chain risk and verifying checksum.
mitigation_steps: Rotated dev-console service tokens and disabled ephemeral-token creation for sessions without step-up MFA.
Blocked ASN 185.239.0.0/16 at network edge and added to WAF denylist pending vendor coordination.
Forced SSO reauth for all org sessions created between 2026-03-13T09:00Z and 2026-03-13T10:30Z.
Scoped CI runners to deny outbound to non-allowlisted external endpoints and quarantined artifacts from the three suspicious builds.
Raised vendor incident with push provider; requested logs and API key usage audit for provider-key-zzx.
Notified legal and compliance; preparing internal communication for impacted employees asking for device review and MFA posture check.
resolution: Ongoing. Immediate mitigations implemented; vendor coordination in progress. Security will update once vendor provides provider-key usage logs and CI artifact verification completes. Post-incident action items to follow for hardening dev-console token creation flow.
follow_up_actions: Add MFA step-up requirement for token creation APIs (owner: Dev Console)
Vendor audit for push provider API keys (owner: Security)
Add CI runner egress allowlist and artifact verification pipeline (owner: CI Infra)
